findings.evidence: Never alter evidence lists evidence bans, not a Gotchas section of environment facts
findings.fix: Add a short Gotchas list for cases the rules do not already decide, such as a quotation that itself contains a cue phrase, or a house style that requires title case.

findings.evidence: description: Edit existing drafts to remove formulaic AI-like prose... Not for authorship detection, factual research, translation, spelling-only proofreading, or writing from scratch.
findings.fix: Edit existing drafts to remove formulaic AI-like prose, promotional puffery and hype, vague attributions, inflated significance and repetitive sentence patterns while preserving facts, quotations, author voice and house style. Use when a draft sounds robotic, generic, salesy or breathless, or the user asks to humanize text, tone down hype, make copy more natural or factual, or remove AI writing patterns, chatbot phrasing, clichés or em-dash overuse, even without mentioning AI. Not for authorship detection, factual research, translation, spelling-only proofreading, or writing from scratch.

findings.evidence: Load `references/pattern-catalog.md` when the text shows chatbot correspondence... Do not load it for a narrow edit whose issue is already listed above.
findings.fix: Name the sections to open for each cue (Correspondence and disclaimers, Vocabulary by model era, Style and mechanics) so a narrow vocabulary edit does not load the whole catalog.

findings.evidence: When depth is unspecified, default to the minimal consequential edit
findings.fix: State what the default change note must contain when the user gives no depth, so the escape hatch is one sentence rather than a judgment call.

findings.evidence: Never replace every em dash or flagged word mechanically: Wikipedia reports that mid-2026 output uses more commas and periods and shorter sentences around a strict 8-20 word limit (it cites one third-party review)
